body: For PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2 and NH3 the sub-index uses the 24-hour average concentration. A 24-hour average is only valid when at least 16 hours of monitored data are available for that day.
For ozone (O3) and carbon monoxide (CO) the sub-index uses the maximum 8-hour average concentration in the day, not the 24-hour average.
The overall AQI is the highest sub-index. It can only be calculated when data for at least three pollutants are available, and one of them must be PM2.5 or PM10.

Each pollutant concentration is converted to a sub-index between 0 and 500 by linear interpolation inside fixed breakpoint bands: Good 0-50, Satisfactory 51-100, Moderately polluted 101-200, Poor 201-300, Very poor 301-400, Severe 401-500.

source: CAG audit report on Delhi air pollution, tabled 1 April 2025 (quoted by ThePrint)
body: Requisite data of concentration of pollutants in the air for a minimum of 16 hours in a day were not available with the DPCC for proper air quality monitoring, so the AQI is not a reliable measure.

source: CAG audit report on Delhi air pollution, as reported by Newslaundry, 1 April 2025
body: The location of continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations did not fulfil CPCB siting requirements, indicating possible inaccuracies in the data generated by them, rendering the AQI values unreliable.
After midnight on Diwali, 21 October 2025, 28 of 39 pollution monitors in Delhi went blank, and hundreds of hours of October PM2.5 data were missing at some stations.

A reading outside the physically possible range for its pollutant, such as zero, a negative error code like -9999, or an absurdly large value from a unit error, is excluded and the day is marked suspect.
When a sensor reports exactly the same hourly value for several hours in a row it is probably frozen. Those hours are excluded from averages and the day is marked suspect.
A change between consecutive hours that is larger than the physical limit for that pollutant is treated as an impossible jump and the day is marked suspect.
The naive AQI is what a dashboard shows when it averages every value it received without checking coverage, plausibility or stuck sensors.
